facts.statement: The discovery of Mansourasaurus was significant because few Late Cretaceous sauropod remains had been found in Africa.
facts.quote: The discovery of Mansourasaurus was considered quite significant by paleontologists, because very few Late Cretaceous sauropod remains have been found in Africa

facts.statement: In 2016, reports indicated that over thirty dinosaur specimens, including titanosaurian sauropods, had been excavated.
facts.quote: In 2016, it was reported that over thirty dinosaur specimens had been excavated, among them titanosaurian sauropods

facts.statement: The generic name Mansourasaurus refers to Mansoura University.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the Mansoura University

facts.statement: The specific name shahinae honors Mona Shahin, a founder of the Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Mona Shahin, one of the founders of the Mansoura University Vertebrate Paleontology Center

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton including a skull and lower jaws.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton with skull and lower jaws

facts.statement: Researchers concluded the holotype was a juvenile because its shoulder girdle bones had not yet fused.
facts.quote: The authors concluded that the holotype is a juvenile specimen because the bones of its shoulder girdle had not yet fused

facts.statement: Mansourasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 83 and 70 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace entre 83 a 70 millones de años durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy África

facts.statement: The animal probably weighed about 5,000 kg, similar to a bull African elephant.
facts.quote: It probably weighed about 5,000 kg, approximately the same as a bull African elephant

facts.statement: Each lower jaw dentary bears ten teeth.
facts.quote: Each lower jaw dentary bears ten teeth

facts.statement: Where the lower jaws meet at the front, they possess a common chin equaling one-third of the front height.
facts.quote: Where the dentaries touch each other, at the front of the lower jaws, they possess a common "chin", equalling a third of the front height

facts.statement: Mansourasaurus is classified within Titanosauria as a derived sister species to Lohuecotitan.
facts.quote: Mansourasaurus was placed in the Titanosauria in a derived position as a sister species of Lohuecotitan

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Mansourasaurus in a clade with largely Eurasian sauropods including Ampelosaurus, Lirainosaurus, Nemegtosaurus, Opisthocoelicaudia, and Paludititan.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis showed it to belong to a clade of otherwise largely Eurasian sauropods, also including Ampelosaurus, Lirainosaurus, Nemegtosaurus, Opisthocoelicaudia, and Paludititan

facts.statement: The existence of Mansourasaurus suggests Africa was less isolated from Eurasian landmasses than previously assumed.
facts.quote: Its existence would show that the continent was far less isolated from the various Eurasian landmasses than had been assumed

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the ancestors of Mansourasaurus reached Africa from Europe.
facts.quote: The ancestors of Mansourasaurus would have reached Africa from Europe

facts.statement: Mansourasaurus is classified as an advanced Titanosauria and is the sister genus to Lohuecotitan.
facts.quote: Mansourasaurus fue clasificado dentro de los Titanosauria en una posición avanzada como un género hermano de Lohuecotitan.

facts.statement: Mansourasaurus is the best-known continental African titanosaur from the Late Cretaceous, specifically the period following the Cenomanian.
facts.quote: Mansourasaurus es el titanosaurio africano continental mejor conocido (es decir, sin incluir a Madagascar) del Cretácico Superior, en particular de la época que sigue al Cenomaniense.

facts.statement: Hypotheses regarding the relationships between Late Cretaceous African and Eurasian sauropods are difficult to test because very few remains have been found in Africa.
facts.quote: Las hipótesis acerca de las relaciones entre los saurópodos africanos y euroasiáticos del Cretácico Superior son difíciles de poner a prueba, debido a que se he han hallado muy pocos de sus restos en África.

facts.statement: Mansourasaurus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Mansourasaurus is Diamantinasauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Diamantinasauria

facts.statement: Mansourasaurus belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia
